338589.title: Zeta-polynomial conjecture for m-divisible odd noncrossing partitions
338589.statement:
For $m\geq 1$, let $C=(x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_m)$ be an $m$-multichain in $\mathcal{O\!N\C}_{2n+1}$, with extended delta sequence $\delta_o(C)=(d_0;d_1,d_2,\ldots,d_m)$ defined by $x_0=e$, $x_{m+1}=c$, and $d_i=x_i^{-1}x_{i+1}$. Define $\mathcal{O\!N\C}_{2n+1}^{(m)}$ by $C\leq C'$ if and only if $d_i\geq_{\mathbf{3}}d_i'$ for $i\in[m]$. **Zeta-polynomial conjecture.** For $n,m\geq 1$, the zeta polynomial of $\mathcal{O\!N\C}_{2n+1}^{(m)}$ is

$$
\mathcal{Z}\bigl(\mathcal{O\!N\C}_{2n+1}^{(m)},q\bigr)=\frac{m(q-1)+1}{(2m(q-1)+1)n+m(q-1)+1}\binom{(2m(q-1)+1)n+m(q-1)+1}{n}.
$$

This conjecture gives an explicit enumeration of multichains in the $m$-divisible odd noncrossing-partition poset; the source provides no resolution or further evidence.

338652.title: Gromov's bounded-imbalance conjecture for planar geodesic nets
338652.statement:
Let $G=(B,U,E)$ be a geodesic net in the plane, with balanced vertices $B$ and unbalanced vertices $U$. For a vertex $v$, let $\operatorname{imb}(v)$ denote the norm of the sum of the unit tangent vectors to the incident edges. For $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $c\in\mathbb{R}$, the total imbalance is $\sum_{v\in U}\operatorname{imb}(v)$. **Gromov's conjecture.** There is a function

$$
g:\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{N}
$$

such that every geodesic net $G=(B,U,E)$ in the plane with $|U|\leq n$ and

$$
\sum_{v\in U}\operatorname{imb}(v)\leq c
$$

has $|B|\leq g(n,c)$. This is presented as an equivalent formulation of Gromov's question about bounding balanced vertices. The paper does not establish the bound in general, so the conjecture remains open.

338655.title: The nullity conjecture for connected block graphs with blocks of order at least 3
338655.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected **block graph**, meaning a graph in which every biconnected component is a clique. The **nullity** of $G$ is the dimension of the kernel of its adjacency matrix.

**Nullity conjecture.** If each block of $G$ has order at least $3$, then the nullity of $G$ is at most $1$.

This conjecture concerns the adjacency-matrix nullity of $K_2$-forbidden block graphs. Its resolution is not indicated in the source.

338716.title: The classification conjecture for unsplittable cyclic $(n_3)$ configurations

338718.title: Conjecture on hard square tiling enumeration
338718.statement:
Let ${\bf T}$ be a finite set of polyomino tiles on the square grid, with copies restricted to parallel translations. A tiling of $[n\times n]$ with ${\bf T}$ is a covering by translated tiles without overlap. The class $\#\mathrm{EXP}$ consists of counting problems for objects verifiable in exponential time.

**Square-tiling hardness conjecture.** There exists a finite set of tiles ${\bf T}$ such that counting the number of tilings of $[n\times n]$ with ${\bf T}$ is $\#\mathrm{EXP}$-complete.

This conjecture predicts exponential-hierarchy counting hardness even for square regions and a fixed tile set. The surrounding discussion emphasizes known hardness for general and slim regions, but gives no proof of the square-region claim.

338739.title: AMRZ conjecture on graph lines and universal pairs
338739.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a connected graph with at least two vertices. Let $\ell(G)$ be the number of distinct graph-metric lines, and let a **universal pair** be a pair of vertices generating a line equal to $V$; write $\textsc{up}(G)$ for the number of universal pairs. **AMRZ's conjecture.**

$$
\ell(G)+\textsc{up}(G)\geq |V|.
$$

The paper proves this inequality for metric spaces whose distances lie in $\{0,1,2\}$, while the stated conjecture for connected graphs in general remains open.

338779.title: Broersma's induced-net Hamiltonicity conjecture
338779.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and call the connected graph with degree sequence $3,3,3,1,1,1$ a **net**, with its vertices of degree $1$ called endvertices. Call $G$ **claw-free** if it has no induced $K_{1,3}$, and let $G$ have order $n$. **Broersma's conjecture.** If $G$ is $2$-connected and every endvertex of each induced net in $G$ has degree at least $\frac{n-2}{3}$, then $G$ is hamiltonian. The conjecture is a degree condition for Hamiltonicity in claw-free graphs and generalizes classical Hamiltonicity results. It was proved in the paper containing this statement.

338841.title: Erde's path-decomposition conjecture for hypercubes
338841.statement: Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube, with edge set of size $n2^{n-1}$. A **path decomposition** of $Q_n$ is a decomposition of its edge set into paths of a common length. **Erde's conjecture.** For even $n$, if $r$ divides $n2^{n-1}$ and $r<2^n$, then a path of length $r$ decomposes $Q_n$. The conjecture generalizes known path decompositions arising from cycle decompositions; the source proves the cases $r=2n,4n,\ldots,2^{m-1}n$ when $n\geq 2^m$, but the full statement remains open.

338842.title: Ramras's fundamental-set conjecture for paths in hypercubes
338842.statement: Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube and let $\operatorname{Aut}(Q_n)$ denote its automorphism group. A subset $F$ of $E(Q_n)$ is a **fundamental set** with respect to a subgroup $\mathcal G\leq\operatorname{Aut}(Q_n)$ if the family $\{g(F):g\in\mathcal G\}$ forms a decomposition of $Q_n$. **Ramras's conjecture.** For an even $n\geq 4$, the edge set of a path of length $2n$ is a fundamental set for $Q_n$. The paper notes that its decomposition result gives the case $r=2n$ of the associated path-decomposition statement, partially resolving this conjecture; the remaining fundamental-set assertion is open.

338852.title: Permutation gauging conjecture for dyslectic modules in type $A_1$
338852.statement: Let $N$ be a positive integer, and let ${\mathcal{C}}$ be the modular tensor category of dyslectic $\mathbf{1} \oplus ((4N-1)\Lambda_1)$-modules in ${\mathcal{C}}(\mathfrak{sl}_2,4N)$. Recall that ${\mathcal{C}}^\text{rev}$ denotes the category monoidally equivalent to ${\mathcal{C}}$ with the reverse braiding. **Permutation gauging conjecture.** The $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ permutation gauging of ${\mathcal{C}}$ is braided equivalent to the category of dyslectic $\mathbf{1} \oplus (4\Lambda_1)$-modules in ${\mathcal{C}}(\mathfrak{so}_{2N+4},4)^\text{rev}$. This predicts the pattern suggested by the examples with $N=2$ and $N=3$; the supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

338951.title: Nonsolvability conjecture for the three-column restricted maze class
338951.statement: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be the class of all mazes, and let $\mathcal{N}_3\subset\mathcal{M}$ be the set of mazes for which the only horizontal edges removed between the pairs of columns $(c_{-4},c_{-3})$ and $(c_3,c_4)$ are HNEs. **Three-column restricted nonsolvability conjecture.** There is no algorithm that solves $\mathcal{N}_3$. The paper presents this as a stronger proposed negative result and does not resolve it.

338965.title: Quadratic-threshold conjecture for near-perfect poset packings
338965.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite poset. A **$P$-packing** is a family of disjoint copies of $P$. Let $c$ be an absolute constant, and consider the truncated Boolean lattice $2^{[n]}-\{\emptyset,[n]\}$.

**Quadratic near-perfect packing conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$ such that, if

$$
n\geq c|P|^2,
$$

then $2^{[n]}-\{\emptyset,[n]\}$ has a $P$-packing that covers all but at most $|P|-1$ elements.

This conjecture strengthens the paper's proved bound for the corresponding near-perfect packing result, replacing the tower-type threshold obtained in the proof by a quadratic one. It remains open.

338996.title: The finite-character-subset conjecture for perfect phylogenies
338996.statement:
Let $X$ be a finite set of taxa. An $r$-state character on $X$ is a partition of $X$ into at most $r$ states. A set $C$ of characters is **compatible** if there is a tree on $X$ that displays every character in $C$; such a tree is a perfect phylogeny for $C$.

**Finite-character-subset conjecture.** For each positive integer $r$, there exists an integer $f(r)$ such that, for any finite set $X$ and any set $C$ of $r$-state characters on $X$, $C$ is compatible if and only if every subset of at most $f(r)$ characters in $C$ is compatible.

This conjecture formalizes the question of whether compatibility can always be determined by checking character subsets of bounded size, independently of the total number of characters. The paper states that the conjecture is false, so it is refuted.

339031.title: (5,2)-cycle-cover conjecture for bridgeless graphs
339031.statement:
Let $G$ be a bridgeless graph, not necessarily cubic. An even subgraph is a subgraph in which every vertex has even degree.

**$(5,2)$-cycle-cover conjecture.** The graph $G$ contains five even subgraphs such that every edge of $G$ belongs to exactly two of them.

The conjecture is presented as a classical consequence of the Petersen coloring conjecture. The supplied source gives no evidence that it has been resolved.

339077.title: The three-shifted q-Motzkin determinant conjecture
339077.statement:
Let $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\dagger}_n(q)$ be the q-Motzkin polynomials defined recursively above, and let

$$
t_n(q)=\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}q^{3k}.
$$

**Three-shift conjecture.** We have

$$
\left(\det\left[\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\dagger}_{i+j+3}(q)\right]_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\right)_{n=1}^{\infty}=\bigl((-1)^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}q^{c_n}f_n(q)\bigr)_{n=1}^{\infty}
$$

for some $c_n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}$ and $g_n(q)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}[q]$. Moreover, if $n\equiv1\pmod3$, then $g_n(q)=(q+1)^2t_n(q)^2$, and if $n\equiv2\pmod3$, then $t_n(q)$ divides $g_n(q)$.
The claim is presented as a numerical conjecture following related determinant identities; the notation $f_n(q)$ is inherited from the preceding conjecture, and no resolution is given.

339078.title: Positivity of even-shifted q-Motzkin Hankel determinants
339078.statement:
Let $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\dagger}_n(q)$ be the q-Motzkin polynomials defined recursively by

$$
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\dagger}_{n+1}(q)=\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\dagger}_n(q)+\sum_{r=0}^{n-1}q^{r+1}\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\dagger}_r(q)\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\dagger}_{n-r-1}(q),\qquad \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\dagger}_0(q)=1.
$$

**Positivity conjecture.** For any $k,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, we have

$$
\det\left[\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\dagger}_{i+j+2k}(q)\right]_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}[q].
$$

This generalizes the preceding shifted-determinant experiments; the source gives no proof or resolution.

339107.title: The plane-partition cell-count conjecture for amplituhedron triangulations
339107.statement:
Let $M(a,b,c)$ denote the number of plane partitions fitting in an $a\times b\times c$ box, namely

$$
M(a,b,c):=\prod_{p=1}^a\prod_{q=1}^b\prod_{r=1}^c \frac{p+q+r-1}{p+q+r-2}.
$$

Let $Z\in\operatorname{Gr}_{>0}(k+m,n)$ and let $f_1,\dots,f_N\in\tilde{S_n}(-k,n-k)$ be a triangulation of $\mathcal{A}_{n,k,m}(Z)$, with $m$ even. **Plane-partition cell-count conjecture.** The number of cells is

$$
N=M(k,\ell,m/2).
$$

This generalizes the conjectural cell count attributed to the BCFW and related triangulations. The source gives no resolution.

339142.title: FO model checking on FO interpretations of nowhere dense classes
339142.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a **nowhere dense graph class**, and let $\mathcal{D}$ be a graph class **FO interpretable** in $\mathcal{C}$. **FO model-checking conjecture.** The class $\mathcal{D}$ has an FPT algorithm for FO model checking. This conjecture asks whether fixed-parameter tractability of FO model checking extends from nowhere dense classes to all graph classes FO interpretable in them; the source presents it as an explicit conjecture, and no resolution is given.

339156.title: Unique rectification targets in d-complete posets
339156.statement: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a $d$-complete poset and let $\lambda \subseteq \mathcal{P}$ be an order ideal. A rectification target is an increasing $\mathcal{P}$-tableau obtained as the result of rectifying a skew increasing tableau. **Unique rectification target conjecture.** There is an explicitly defined unique rectification target supported on $\lambda$. This conjecture asks whether general $d$-complete posets have enough unique rectification targets to extend the Thomas–Yong jeu de taquin theory beyond minuscule varieties; the precise formulation identifies the target with the minimally labeled tableau described below.

339171.title: The anti-van der Waerden bound for Cartesian products of connected graphs
339171.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be connected graphs, and let $G\square H$ denote their Cartesian product. The anti-van der Waerden number $\operatorname{aw}(G\square H,3)$ is the least positive integer $r$ such that every exact $r$-coloring of $G\square H$ contains a rainbow $3$-term arithmetic progression.

**Cartesian-product anti-van der Waerden conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{aw}(G\square H,3)\le 4.
$$

This conjecture gives a uniform upper bound on the number of colors needed to force a rainbow $3$-term arithmetic progression in the Cartesian product of any two connected graphs. The supplied material does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
